day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight KL lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Take the Amsterdam Airport Express (Sprinter train) from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (~17 min, €5.40). Check in to Canal House Amsterdam and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate neighbourhood on foot. Stroll along the Herengracht and Prinsengracht canals near the hotel to get your bearings. Visit the nearby Westerkerk (Western Church) — free to enter the grounds — and admire the tower that Anne Frank wrote about in her diary. Browse the Jordaan district's charming streets and independent boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Leidseplein square (15–20 min) to soak up the lively street atmosphere and buskers. Grab dinner at a local spot and wind down after the journey.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick Dutch broodje (sandwich) or stroopwafel from a street stall near Amsterdam Centraal on arrival (~€3–5)
meals.dinner: Moeders restaurant in the Jordaan — hearty Dutch home-cooking, mains ~€14–18. Alternatively, pick up a kapsalon or falafel wrap from a Leidseplein takeaway for ~€6–8

day_by_day.notes: Buy a multi-day GVB transit card (3-day pass ~€17) at the airport or Centraal station — it covers trams, buses and metro and will save money across the trip. Pre-book the Anne Frank House online as soon as possible; timed-entry tickets sell out weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour (9:00–10:30 recommended slot — book timed entry in advance, €16 adult). Arrive early to beat crowds. The hidden annex is a deeply moving 60–90 minute experience. Afterward, pause at the statue of Anne Frank on Westermarkt square.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Rijksmuseum (tram 2/12 from Leidseplein, ~10 min, or a 25-min walk through the Jordaan). Spend 2–3 hours exploring Rembrandt's Night Watch, Vermeer's The Milkmaid, and Dutch Golden Age masterpieces. Book tickets online in advance to save queuing time (€22.50 adult). Stroll through Museumplein and relax by the iconic 'I Amsterdam' letters area.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or tram to the Albert Cuyp Market area (open until ~17:00 on Saturdays) for cheap street snacks. Explore the vibrant De Pijp neighbourhood for dinner. Return to the hotel via tram.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh bread, cheese and fruit from a local Albert Heijn supermarket near the hotel (~€3–4) — great budget hack
meals.lunch: Herring (haring) from a street cart near the Rijksmuseum or a Dutch pancake (pannenkoek) at a local café (~€5–8)
meals.dinner: Warung Spang-Makandra in De Pijp — authentic Surinamese-Javanese cuisine, filling mains ~€10–13

day_by_day.notes: The Rijksmuseum is free for visitors under 18. The museum's garden (Rijksmuseum Gardens) is free to enter and lovely in May. Wear comfortable shoes — you'll walk 8–10 km today.

day_by_day.morning: Van Gogh Museum Experience (open from 09:00; book timed-entry tickets online, €22 adult). Arrive at opening to enjoy the galleries before the afternoon crowds. Spend 1.5–2 hours with Sunflowers, The Bedroom, and Almond Blossom. The museum covers Van Gogh's full artistic journey chronologically.
day_by_day.afternoon: Canal Ring Boat Tour — depart from a dock near the Rijksmuseum or Leidseplein (~€15–18 for a 1-hour guided cruise with companies like Blue Boat or Amsterdam Canal Cruises; look for online discount codes for ~€12). Glide past 17th-century merchant houses, the Magere Brug drawbridge, and the UNESCO-listed canal ring. After the cruise, explore the Bloemenmarkt (floating flower market) on the Singel canal — free to browse.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Begijnhof, a hidden medieval courtyard garden — free entry, closes around 17:00, so aim to arrive by 16:30. Then wander the Nine Streets (De 9 Straatjes) for window-shopping. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in the city centre.

meals.breakfast: Supermarket staples from Albert Heijn or Jumbo (~€3–4), or a fresh stroopwafel and coffee from a market stall (~€3)
meals.lunch: Vleminckx Sausmeesters — legendary Amsterdam frites (fries) with sauce near the Bloemenmarkt (~€4–5). A true Amsterdam institution.
meals.dinner: Café 't Smalle in the Jordaan — classic Dutch brown café with affordable bitterballen, toasties and soup (~€8–12 for a light meal and a local beer)

day_by_day.notes: Sunday mornings are quieter at the Van Gogh Museum. The Canal Ring Boat Tour is best in afternoon light. Tipping in Amsterdam is appreciated but not mandatory — rounding up the bill is the norm.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Amsterdam Museum or the Amsterdam City Archives (Stadsarchief) — the latter is free and housed in a stunning 1926 building with fascinating rotating exhibitions on city history. Alternatively, explore the Jewish Historical Museum and the Portuguese Synagogue in the Jewish Quarter (~€17 combined ticket) for rich WWII and pre-war cultural history that complements the Anne Frank experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (OV-fiets with your transit card ~€3.85/day, or rental shops from ~€10/day) and cycle along the Eastern Docklands (Oostelijke Eilanden) — a striking neighbourhood of modern architecture contrasting with historic warehouses. Visit the NEMO Science Museum exterior (free) for panoramic rooftop views over the city. Cycle back along the IJ waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Amsterdam's lively Nieuwmarkt square and the surrounding Chinatown area. Visit the Waag (medieval weigh house) at dusk for great photos. Browse the evening atmosphere around Rembrandtplein.

meals.breakfast: Dampkring café or any local bakery near the hotel for a coffee and croissant (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Broodje Bert or similar local sandwich shop near the Jewish Quarter — fresh Dutch sandwiches ~€5–7
meals.dinner: New King restaurant in Chinatown near Nieuwmarkt — generous portions of Chinese-Dutch cuisine ~€10–14. One of Amsterdam's best-value sit-down dinners.

day_by_day.notes: Cycling is the most authentic Amsterdam experience and the fastest way to cover ground. Always lock your bike with two locks. The Eastern Docklands route is flat and very beginner-friendly. NEMO rooftop is free and one of the best viewpoints in the city.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — visit the Vondelpark (free), Amsterdam's beloved green lung. Rent a rowing boat on the park pond (~€10/hour) or simply enjoy a coffee at one of the park cafés. Browse the weekend antique and book markets if still running. Walk or cycle to the Stedelijk Museum (modern and contemporary art, €22.50) if you want one last museum hit, or opt for the free EYE Film Museum across the IJ (free ferry from behind Centraal station — the ferry itself is a free scenic mini-cruise).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Albert Cuyp Market or the Waterlooplein Flea Market (open Mon–Sat, free entry) for affordable Dutch keepsakes — stroopwafels, Delft-style ceramics, vintage finds. Pack up at the hotel and head to Amsterdam Centraal for the Schiphol Express back to the airport (allow 90 minutes before your flight).
day_by_day.evening: Departure — allow ample time for Schiphol security (arrive at airport 2–2.5 hours before flight). Grab a final Dutch bitterbal or apple pie at a Schiphol café as a farewell treat.

meals.breakfast: Café Vertigo inside Vondelpark — lovely terrace setting, coffee and eggs ~€7–10
meals.lunch: Grab a Dutch broodje or warm stroopwafel from the Albert Cuyp Market street stalls (~€4–6) — the ultimate budget Amsterdam lunch
meals.dinner: Airport meal at Schiphol or a light snack before departure (~€8–12 budget)

day_by_day.notes: The free GVB ferry from Amsterdam Centraal to the EYE Film Museum (Noord side) takes 5 minutes and gives a wonderful view of the city skyline — highly recommended even if you don't visit the museum. Keep your GVB transit card topped up for the Schiphol train journey. Total estimated trip spend (excluding flights and hotel): approx. €150–180 covering all admissions, meals, and local transport.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In — Flight KL lands at 13:00. Take the Amsterdam Airport Express (Sprinter) from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (~17 min, €5). Transfer by tram or taxi to Canal House Amsterdam. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a leisurely stroll along the nearby canals to shake off travel fatigue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Canal Ring Boat Tour — At around 15:00, join a guided boat tour of Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed 17th-century canal ring. Departing from a central dock near Centraal Station (a short tram ride away), the 1.5-hour cruise offers a perfect first introduction to the city — gliding past gabled merchant houses, historic bridges, and the Jordaan district from the water. Book a slot in advance to secure your preferred time.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Leidseplein & Surrounding Streets — Wander to the lively Leidseplein square for your first taste of Amsterdam's evening atmosphere. Browse the surrounding streets before settling in for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and stroopwafel or a light snack at Schiphol Airport before or after landing — no formal breakfast scheduled given the midday arrival.
meals.lunch: Café Loetje (near Jordaan) — a beloved Amsterdam institution known for its excellent medium-rare steak sandwiches and Dutch-style brown café ambiance. Budget ~€15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Café de Reiger (Jordaan neighborhood) — a classic Dutch eetcafé with a seasonal menu, warm candlelit interior, and hearty portions. Mains around €18–26. Reserve ahead as it fills quickly on weekends.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Allow buffer time for baggage, transit, and check-in before starting activities. The Canal Boat Tour is the perfect low-energy, high-reward first activity. Tram lines 1, 2, and 5 connect most central attractions from the hotel area.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit — Arrive at opening (9:00) to beat the crowds. Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring the Netherlands' premier museum, home to Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch,' Vermeer's 'The Milkmaid,' and thousands of Dutch Golden Age masterpieces. Pre-book timed entry tickets online (~€22.50). The museum is a 15-minute tram ride from the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum Experience — Just a 5-minute walk from the Rijksmuseum, head to the Van Gogh Museum after lunch. Spend 1.5–2 hours immersing yourself in the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works, including 'Sunflowers,' 'The Bedroom,' and 'Almond Blossom.' Pre-book tickets (~€22). Afterward, relax in the adjacent Vondelpark — Amsterdam's beloved green lung — perfect for a mid-afternoon recharge.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in De Pijp neighborhood — Amsterdam's vibrant multicultural quarter, a 10-minute walk from Vondelpark. Browse the Albert Cuyp Market area (closes ~17:00 on weekdays, check Saturday hours) before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Buffet or continental breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam or nearby Scandinavian Embassy café — known for exceptional specialty coffee and open-faced sourdough sandwiches (~€10–14).
meals.lunch: Museumplein area — grab a Dutch kroket or broodje (sandwich) from a local bakery or the Rijksmuseum's own café garden for a relaxed outdoor lunch. Budget ~€10–15.
meals.dinner: Brasserie Harkema (Nes Street, De Pijp adjacent) or Brouwerij 't IJ tap room for craft beer and bites — alternatively, try Momo Amsterdam for Asian-European fusion at mid-range prices (~€25–35 per person with drinks).

day_by_day.notes: Saturday can be busy at both museums — timed entry tickets are essential and should be booked at least a week in advance. Wear comfortable shoes as this is a walking-heavy museum day. Vondelpark is especially lovely in May with spring blooms.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour — This is Amsterdam's most emotionally significant site and requires advance booking (tickets sell out weeks ahead, ~€16). Aim for a 9:00 or 10:00 timed slot to avoid peak crowds. Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid for over two years during WWII. Allow 1.5 hours and go with an open, reflective mindset — it is a profoundly moving experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Walking & Food Tour — Transitioning from reflection to discovery, join a guided cultural and culinary walking tour of the Jordaan, Amsterdam's most picturesque bohemian neighborhood — conveniently located right next to the Anne Frank House. The tour typically covers hidden courtyards (hofjes), independent galleries, street art, and tastings of Dutch cheeses, herring, and local bites. Duration ~2.5–3 hours. Cost ~€35–55 per person.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Canal Walk & Drinks — As evening approaches, take a self-guided stroll along the Prinsengracht and Herengracht canals. In May, golden hour light on the canal houses is spectacular. Stop at a waterside terrace bar for a local Heineken, Amstel, or jenever (Dutch gin).

meals.breakfast: Winkel 43 (Noordermarkt, Jordaan) — famous for its apple pie and a Sunday farmers' market outside. Arrive before 10:00 for shorter queues. Budget ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Included tastings during the Jordaan Food Tour — supplemented by a fresh herring (haring) from a street cart if still hungry (~€4–5). A true Amsterdam rite of passage.
meals.dinner: Toscanini (Lindengracht, Jordaan) — a beloved Italian restaurant with an open kitchen and convivial atmosphere, popular with locals. Pasta and mains ~€18–28. Reserve well in advance as it's consistently packed.

day_by_day.notes: The Anne Frank House MUST be pre-booked — walk-up tickets are rarely available. Sunday mornings in the Jordaan are magical with the Noordermarkt organic and antique markets running simultaneously. The food tour and Anne Frank visit pair naturally as they are within walking distance of each other.

day_by_day.morning: Amsterdam Museum Quarter & Stedelijk Museum — Begin the morning at the Stedelijk Museum (~€22.50), Amsterdam's world-class modern and contemporary art museum, located on Museumplein. Explore works by Mondrian, Kandinsky, and Matisse, plus rotating contemporary exhibitions. A quieter, more contemplative contrast to the Rijksmuseum. Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day Excursion to Haarlem or Keukenhof (May is peak tulip season) — Take a 15-minute train from Amsterdam Centraal to Haarlem (~€5 each way). Explore the charming medieval city center, the Grote Kerk cathedral, and the Frans Hals Museum. Alternatively, if tulips are still blooming, Keukenhof Gardens (open until ~mid-May) is a short bus ride from Schiphol and is a stunning seasonal experience (~€20 entry). Check bloom status closer to your travel date.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Amsterdam & Red Light District Cultural Walk — Take an evening walk through the historic De Wallen (Red Light District) — approached as a cultural and historical experience rather than just nightlife. The area contains Amsterdam's oldest church (Oude Kerk, dating to 1213) and fascinating layers of city history. Join a guided evening walking tour for deeper context (~€15–20).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Lot Sixty One Coffee Roasters (Kinkerstraat) — one of Amsterdam's top specialty coffee shops with excellent pastries. Budget ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: In Haarlem: Lunch at a local café on the Grote Markt square — try stamppot (Dutch mashed potato dish) or a seasonal salad at a traditional eetcafé. Budget ~€14–18.
meals.dinner: Gartine (Taksteeg, Amsterdam city center) — a charming hidden gem open for dinner, known for seasonal Dutch cuisine using garden-grown produce. Set menus ~€30–38. Intimate and highly recommended. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: May is one of the best months to visit Keukenhof (open late March–mid-May) — confirm exact closing dates for 2027 as they vary slightly year to year. If Keukenhof has closed, Haarlem is an excellent alternative day trip. Monday tends to be quieter at most Amsterdam museums.

day_by_day.morning: Amsterdam Historical Museum (Amsterdam Museum) & Begijnhof — Begin with a visit to the Amsterdam Museum (currently undergoing renovation — check 2027 status) or head directly to the nearby Begijnhof, a serene 14th-century courtyard of almshouses hidden in the city center. One of Amsterdam's most peaceful and photogenic spots. Afterward, explore the Spui square and its Tuesday book market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dutch Cheese & Jenever Tasting + Free Exploration — Visit a traditional Dutch cheese shop such as Henri Willig or a local proeflokal (tasting house) like Wynand Fockink (est. 1679) near Dam Square for a jenever (Dutch gin) tasting flight (~€10–15). Spend the remaining afternoon at leisure — revisit a favorite canal, browse independent boutiques in the Nine Streets (De 9 Straatjes), or simply sit at a canal-side café with a final coffee and stroopwafel.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Canal Nightcap — Celebrate your final evening with a special dinner before a relaxed nightcap along the illuminated canals.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes! Amsterdam — a beloved local spot serving both sweet and savory Dutch pancakes (pannenkoeken). Budget ~€10–15. A perfect final-morning tradition.
meals.lunch: Grab a Dutch-style broodje (sandwich) from Brood (multiple locations) or a fresh bowl at Soup en Zo — Amsterdam's popular soup-and-bread chain. Light, affordable, and local. Budget ~€10–14.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Vinkeles (Dylan Hotel, Keizersgracht) — for a special farewell splurge at the higher end of mid-range: a Michelin-recognized Dutch fine dining experience in a stunning 18th-century canal house bakery. Tasting menus ~€75–95. Alternatively, for a more casual farewell, Rijsel (Marcusstraat) serves excellent French-Belgian rotisserie chicken in a convivial, buzzing atmosphere (~€25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Check departure logistics for Day 6 — Amsterdam Centraal to Schiphol takes ~17 minutes by direct train (runs every 10–15 minutes). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for transit and airport security. The Nine Streets area is ideal for last-minute souvenir shopping — look for Dutch design items, local gin, and artisan chocolate rather than tourist-trap shops near Dam Square.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In: Flight KL lands at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from Amsterdam Airport Schiphol to Canal House Amsterdam via private luxury transfer (pre-book through the hotel concierge). Settle into your canal-view suite and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Canal Ring Boat Tour: After settling in, embark on a private guided boat tour of Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed 17th-century canal ring. Departing from a pier steps from the hotel, glide past Golden Age merchant houses, ornate bridges, and hidden courtyards. Opt for a private vessel with champagne service for the full luxury experience (approx. 2 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Jordaan Neighborhood Stroll & Dinner: Take a leisurely evening walk through the charming Jordaan neighborhood, exploring its narrow lanes, art galleries, and boutique shops. Dine at Restaurant Rijks (adjacent to the Rijksmuseum) or Bord'Eau at Hotel de l'Europe — both offer refined Dutch-French cuisine with outstanding wine lists. Reserve well in advance.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport lounge meal prior to landing)
meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at the hotel or a quick bite at Café Luxembourg on Spui Square — elegant brasserie fare in a grand Art Deco setting
meals.dinner: Bord'Eau at Hotel de l'Europe — Michelin-starred French-Dutch cuisine with stunning Amstel River views; tasting menu with wine pairing recommended

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer with the hotel. Request early check-in if possible. Book the private canal boat and dinner reservation before arrival. The Canal House Amsterdam is ideally located in the Keizersgracht canal belt, making all afternoon and evening activities walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit: Begin the day with a private guided tour of the Rijksmuseum, the Netherlands' premier museum. Marvel at Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch,' Vermeer's 'The Milkmaid,' and Van Dyck's masterworks. A private guide (bookable through the hotel concierge) ensures skip-the-line access and an intimate, curated experience through the Golden Age galleries (2.5–3 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum Experience: A short walk from the Rijksmuseum, immerse yourself in the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works — including 'Sunflowers,' 'The Bedroom,' and 'Almond Blossom.' Book a premium time-slot entry and consider a private docent for deeper insight into Van Gogh's turbulent life and revolutionary technique (2 hours). Afterward, relax in the elegant Museumplein gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Fine Dining in the Museum Quarter: Head to Vinkeles, a Michelin-starred restaurant set within a former 18th-century bakery inside the Dylan Hotel on the Keizersgracht. The intimate setting and innovative Dutch tasting menu make for an unforgettable evening. Pair with a sommelier-selected wine flight.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — expect a lavish spread of artisan breads, smoked salmon, Dutch cheeses, fresh juices, and eggs prepared to order
meals.lunch: Café Cobra in Museumplein — a stylish, art-inspired café perfectly positioned between the two museums; enjoy a premium sandwich, soup, or salad with a glass of Dutch craft beer or wine
meals.dinner: Vinkeles at The Dylan Amsterdam — Michelin-starred tasting menu in a breathtaking historic setting; reserve the chef's table for an exclusive kitchen-side experience

day_by_day.notes: Book Rijksmuseum private guide and Van Gogh Museum premium tickets at least 2–4 weeks in advance, especially for a Saturday. The Museumplein area is approximately a 15-minute walk or short taxi ride from the Canal House Amsterdam. Vinkeles is one of Amsterdam's most sought-after reservations — book as early as possible.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour: Begin with a profoundly moving visit to the Anne Frank House, a short walk from the hotel along the Prinsengracht canal. Book a premium early-morning time slot (8:00–9:00 AM) for the most intimate experience before crowds arrive. Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during WWII, guided by expert audio narration or a private guide. Allow 1.5–2 hours for quiet reflection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Walking & Food Tour: Transition from history to culture with a private guided walking and culinary tour through Amsterdam's most picturesque bohemian neighborhood. Discover hidden courtyards (hofjes), independent galleries, and specialty food purveyors. Sample Dutch cheeses, stroopwafels, raw herring, and artisan chocolates. Your guide will share neighborhood lore and insider recommendations (3 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Canal Aperitivo & Dinner at Pulitzer Amsterdam: Enjoy pre-dinner drinks on the terrace of the Pulitzer Amsterdam hotel bar — a beautifully restored row of 17th-century canal houses. Then dine at Jansz., the Pulitzer's acclaimed restaurant, for modern European cuisine in a warmly lit, art-filled setting.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before the Anne Frank House — fresh pastries, coffee, and fruit to keep it swift
meals.lunch: Included tastings during the Jordaan Food Tour; supplement with a sit-down lunch at Brouwerij 't IJ — Amsterdam's iconic windmill brewery serving artisan beers and elevated Dutch bar snacks
meals.dinner: Jansz. Restaurant at Pulitzer Amsterdam — seasonal European menu with a curated Dutch gin and wine program; ask for a canal-side table

day_by_day.notes: Anne Frank House tickets must be booked online in advance — they sell out weeks ahead, especially on weekends. The 8:00–9:00 AM slot offers the most serene experience. The Jordaan tour and Anne Frank House are both within easy walking distance of the Canal House Amsterdam. Sunday markets (Noordermarkt organic market) may be active nearby — worth a brief detour.

day_by_day.morning: Amsterdam's Golden Age History Deep Dive — Amsterdam Museum & Begijnhof: Spend the morning exploring Amsterdam's layered history. Visit the newly renovated Amsterdam Museum for an immersive journey through the city's evolution from a medieval fishing village to a global trading empire. Afterward, step into the hidden Begijnhof — a tranquil 14th-century courtyard sanctuary in the heart of the city, one of Amsterdam's best-kept secrets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Antique & Art Gallery Tour in the Spiegelkwartier: Spend the afternoon in Amsterdam's prestigious antiques district, the Spiegelkwartier, a short stroll from the Rijksmuseum. Browse world-class galleries and dealers specializing in Dutch Golden Age paintings, Delftware, silver, and vintage maps. Consider arranging a private curator-led tour through the hotel concierge — ideal for collectors or serious culture enthusiasts. Stop at Moooi or Frozen Fountain for cutting-edge Dutch design.
day_by_day.evening: Private Candlelit Dinner Cruise on the Canals: For an unforgettable evening, book a private luxury dinner cruise aboard a beautifully appointed historic canal boat. A personal chef prepares a multi-course Dutch-inspired menu on board as you glide through illuminated canals at dusk. Toast with Dutch gin (jenever) cocktails and fine Champagne as Amsterdam's bridges and gabled houses glow in the evening light.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — take your time with a leisurely spread before a culturally rich day
meals.lunch: Café de Jaren on the Amstel River — a beloved grand café with a stunning riverside terrace; enjoy Dutch-French bistro fare and a glass of white Burgundy
meals.dinner: Private on-board dinner cruise — curated multi-course menu prepared by a private chef; champagne, wine, and jenever pairings included (book through luxury concierge services such as Amsterdam Private Boat Hire or the hotel)

day_by_day.notes: The private dinner cruise should be booked at least 1–2 weeks in advance through a premium operator. The Spiegelkwartier galleries are typically open Monday afternoons. The Begijnhof requests quiet and respectful visiting — no large groups. This day is intentionally less structured to allow for organic discovery and relaxed luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely Farewell Morning — Floating Flower Market & Keukenhof Reflection Walk: Begin with a relaxed stroll to the Bloemenmarkt, Amsterdam's iconic floating flower market on the Singel canal — browse tulip bulbs, Dutch souvenirs, and fresh blooms. Then take a peaceful walk along the Herengracht (the 'Gentleman's Canal'), Amsterdam's most prestigious canal, admiring the grand 17th-century merchant mansions known as the 'Golden Bend.' Stop at the Hermitage Amsterdam area for architecture appreciation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell Luxury Spa Experience & Check-Out: Return to the hotel for a late check-out (negotiate with the hotel in advance) and indulge in a farewell spa treatment — a full-body Dutch botanical massage or hydrotherapy session at the hotel spa or a nearby luxury wellness center such as Sauna Deco (a stunning Art Deco bathhouse). Pack at leisure and enjoy one final canal view from your suite.
day_by_day.evening: Departure Preparation & Farewell Dinner: Depending on your departure flight, enjoy a final celebratory dinner at Restaurant Ciel Bleu on the 23rd floor of Hotel Okura Amsterdam — a two-Michelin-starred restaurant with panoramic city views and an exceptional French-Japanese tasting menu. A fitting, spectacular close to a premium Amsterdam journey. Private transfer to Schiphol Airport arranged through the hotel concierge.

meals.breakfast: Final indulgent breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — order the full Dutch breakfast with smoked eel, aged Gouda, fresh stroopwafels, and a Bellini
meals.lunch: Librije's Zusje at the Waldorf Astoria Amsterdam — set within five interconnected 17th-century canal houses; an elegant Michelin-starred lunch in one of the city's most beautiful dining rooms
meals.dinner: Restaurant Ciel Bleu at Hotel Okura (23rd floor) — two Michelin stars, panoramic Amsterdam skyline views, French-Japanese haute cuisine with an extraordinary wine cellar; the perfect farewell dinner

day_by_day.notes: Confirm late check-out with Canal House Amsterdam upon arrival or during the stay. Book Ciel Bleu and Librije's Zusje well in advance. Arrange the private airport transfer for departure day through the hotel. Purchase tulip bulbs at the Bloemenmarkt as a premium souvenir — they are certified for international travel. Consider a final jenever tasting at Wynand Fockink, a historic 1679 distillery near Dam Square, before heading to the airport.
